assessment.summary: EGFR (P00533) is one of the most extensively validated and drugged targets in oncology, with 393 PDB structures (best resolution 1.07Å), 26,600 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 20 approved drugs including small molecules and biologics. The structural, chemical, and literature evidence collectively place this target in the highest tier of druggability with exceptional confidence across all dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 75.9 with only 70.7% high-confidence residues suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular or linker domains) not well-captured by crystallography — functional relevance of these regions for novel modalities is unclear

Median IC50 of 2000 nM across 26,600 entries is relatively high, suggesting many compounds in the dataset are weak binders; potency distribution and selectivity profiles for next-generation compounds warrant scrutiny

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., T790M, C797S, exon 20 insertions) are well-documented but continued evolution of resistance limits long-term therapeutic durability — no single compound fully addresses all resistance variants
Tissue-specific expression and on-target toxicity (e.g., skin, GI) remain translational challenges not captured in the druggability metrics

Some approved drugs listed may reflect combination or salt forms (e.g., erlotinib HCl, lapatinib ditosylate) rather than distinct chemical entities — true chemical diversity of approved agents may be slightly overstated by the count of 20
